Prevention: Preferred method: transplanting by 25-30 days old seedling
Prevent snails from entering field by filtering the water entering the field through net traps (5 mm mesh).
Clean equipment (especially harvester) before moving into another field to prevent spreading the pest.
Before planting, make drains in the rice field and add water to the drain.
Allow snails to migrate to the water and collect snails and destroy them.
Plant by transplanting rice instead of direct seedling.
Rotate rice with dry land crop and/or allow for fallow periods between flooded rice.
Monitoring: Observe egg mass on rice and weeds around rice field once a week
Adults are yellow-brown to greenish brown or dark chestnut, sometimes with dark brown spiral bands of variable number and thickness. 35-60 mm tall
If pest population density exceeds 5 snails per square meter, use
Direct Control: Put sticks (approximately 300 cm long) in rice field.
Allow snail to lay eggs and then collect and destroy eggs from the stick.
Drain water from the field and collect the snails with basket/net.
Release ducks into the field (5-10 ducks/ha for 1 month).
If low population, catch by hand and destroy or make snail compost.
Organize field days to collect and destroy snails.
Cassava leaves and place them in water along edges of field for at least 24 hours.
When the snails get trapped there, collect and destroy them.
Restrictions: Spray in morning between 6-10 am or in afternoon between 3-6 pm
